turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have about twenty minutes before a client call, so let's start with who decided to give Owen a zero, and whether anyone spoke to him first.
Before anything else: I entered the zero before I called you. That broke procedure 4.2, and I am sorry Owen found out on his phone.
Okay. Then tell me what you have, and what the zero was based on.
Here is the version history. Created Wednesday, October 28, 11:31 PM, title only. At 11:52 PM, 612 words in one edit. At 11:58 PM, 794 more. No earlier drafts. Turn the screen and read it yourself.
I'm writing those times down. Text that appears in big pieces doesn't show where it was written, and Owen told me he wrote it over the weekend. Is that your whole case?
If he drafted it somewhere else, that file has its own dates. Bring it and I will look at it with you. Until then, this is the only history there is.
Okay. Whatever comes of this, it stays off his record and it stays quiet. What else do you have?
Second: the essay quotes Act 3, Scene 2: The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile. Here is the whole play on my screen. Search every edition you like; the line is not in Hamlet.

I'll search it myself. A student can lift a line from a critic or a study guide and pin it on the wrong scene, and that's a mistake, not proof of who wrote it. Did you check whether it comes from a published source?
It is not a misremembered line. There is no line in the play close to it. Search the word exile yourself.
You've told me about the play. I asked about everywhere else, and you haven't said. I'll run the word myself tonight, and what you tell me now goes in writing.
Third: his in-class writing from September 24. 380 words in 40 minutes, comma splices, no quotations. The essay has nine quotations cited by act, scene and line. Here are both, side by side.
I'm reading both. A timed piece in class and an essay written at home are different kinds of writing, and plenty of students do them differently. What's your answer to that?

Under procedure 4.4 this is a first concern. A supervised rewrite, private, not in front of his class. If it shows the learning, its mark replaces the zero and nothing goes on his record. I will put that in writing tonight.

Okay. I'll take the rewrite to put this behind him, and I'm conceding nothing about Owen by it. I want the email tonight, saying it's private, nothing goes on his record, and the zero comes out of the gradebook until the rewrite is marked.
Will he do it?
He'll sit it. I'll tell him tonight, and he does it because I'm asking, not because anyone's proved anything. When is it, and who supervises?
END MEETING

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL

Hale,

You agreed in the meeting to a private, supervised rewrite under your own procedure, with its mark replacing the zero and nothing placed in Owen's record. I still want the zero out of the gradebook until the rewrite is marked, and the date and the name of the supervisor stated in writing. You said you would put it in writing tonight, and I expect it tonight.

Meredith Kalinowski
cc: Principal

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: She reached her last position and accepted a private supervised rewrite with nothing on his record, and she still wants the zero out of the gradebook until it is marked, plus the date and the supervisor in writing; that is the fair outcome under procedure 4.4, and her time did not run out first.
What moved her: You laid out dated documents she could check herself, starting with the version history, and you answered her defence about other files with something she could test.
What cost ground: You never answered her question about whether the quoted line came from a published source, which left her a gap she could use for that piece of evidence.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your version history, with its late-night times the evening before the due date, came very close to that night, though it proves nothing about the essay, and it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: When she asked whether you had checked a published source for the line, answer that directly at that moment, so the point stands instead of being left open.
